description: Arithmetic operators, their zero-guards, and precedence.

cases.name: division by zero yields 0
cases.note: MilkDrop never propagates Infinity out of a division.

cases.name: division by a tiny nonzero divisor divides normally
cases.note: The guard is exact-zero, NOT the close factor. A tolerance guard here zeroes large finite results real presets depend on.

cases.name: the % operator truncates both operands to integers first
cases.note: trunc(7.5) % trunc(0.7) = 7 % 0 = 0. Float remainder is mod()/fmod(), not %.

cases.name: the % operator is trunc-mod, so the sign follows the dividend
mod()/fmod() is a float remainder, unlike the % operator
cases.note: Same trunc-toward-zero sign rule as %, but without truncating the operands.

cases.name: ^ overflow clamps to 0, not Infinity
cases.note: The finite clamp applies to the operator result, not only at the store.

cases.name: a negative base with an integral exponent is real
cases.note: milkdropPow is sign-decomposed on the GPU tiers to match this.

cases.name: a negative base with a fractional exponent is 0 via the NaN clamp
a negative exponent is a reciprocal
unary minus binds LOOSER than ^: -2 ^ 2 is -(2^2)
cases.note: Pinned by the ns-eel2 source (WACUP/vis_milk2@de9625a). nseel-compiler.c:1203 makes `^` a preprocessor rewrite to pow(), and its left-operand scan stops at the first character that is not alphanumeric, `_` or `.` (nseel-compiler.c:1249), so the `-` stays outside: `x = -2^2` becomes `_set(x, -pow(2,2))`. nseel-caltab.c:399 then applies FN_UMINUS to the whole pow() call: -4. Modern EEL2 disagrees: WDL's eel2.y puts unary_expr inside pow_expr's operand (`pow_expr: pow_expr '^' unary_expr`), so -2^2 is +4 there. This corpus specifies MilkDrop 2's dialect, so the ns-eel2 reading is the pin; an engine that follows WDL will fail this case by design. No bundled preset writes -a^b, -(a)^b or -f(a)^b, so the correction changed no preset. Until 2026-10-28 this case was provisional and pinned +4.

cases.name: ^ is LEFT-associative
cases.note: Pinned by both references. In ns-eel2 (WACUP/vis_milk2@de9625a) the right-operand scan stops at the next operator once it has seen an operand (nseel-compiler.c:1313), and the left scan of the following `^` takes the finished pow() call whole, so `2^3^2` becomes `pow(pow(2,3),2)` (verified by running the extracted preprocessor), and modern EEL2's grammar is left-recursive (`pow_expr: pow_expr '^' unary_expr`, WDL eel2.y). (2^3)^2 = 64, not the right-associative 512 most languages would give. Provisional until 2026-10-28; the value did not change.
